why:
creates the entity in a named callback group, so its callbacks run on the tier that group maps to (RFC-0002). rclcpp passes the group through `PublisherOptions` instead. The publisher form accepts the group for API symmetry and has no scheduling effect -- a publisher has no dispatched callback (RFC-0047 OQ1 follow-up).

phase-427 (the `_in_group` split) -- this row was `cpp:Node::create_publisher_in` until the suffix carried two meanings on one class. `_in` now means the ours-only, storage-free shape; `_in_group` means the first parameter is a `CallbackGroup`. See RFC-0089, "The `_in` rule, amended", and the ours-only row `cpp:Node::create_publisher_in`.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-17, third of three: THE GROUP IS DROPPED. `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/node.hpp:847` takes the `CallbackGroup&` as an UNNAMED parameter and forwards to plain `create_publisher<M>(out, topic, qos)`. The sibling `create_subscription_in_group` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/subscription.hpp:728`) really does pass `ffi_options.callback_group = group.get_name()`, so the two verbs that read as a pair behave differently.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG — it compiles, returns ok, and the publisher runs outside the group named in the call. It IS documented at the method (`node.hpp:835`, API symmetry with no scheduling effect, RFC-0047 OQ1), which is why this is an amendment and not a new finding; recorded because "documented inert" is exactly the deferral RFC-0089 exists to end.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and this verb is ours: rclcpp passes the callback group through `PublisherOptions` and has no `create_publisher_in_group`, so there is no upstream candidate for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse. What the finding asks for is that the parameter either work or not be accepted, which is a correctness question rather than an adoption decision.
